verdicts.decisive_quote: While Q4 2024 showed strength, the muted outlook implies that the factors driving growth may not sustain a rate of at least 20.63% year-over-year for Q1 2025.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Cleanest chain in the set: every qualitative claim traces to an E0 headline, the competing 'strong Q4 vs muted outlook' signals are explicitly resolved against the demanding threshold, and the modest 0.7/0.3 split matches the declared 'insufficient' magnitude support, though the 5/15/25 percent band is an unanchored assertion.

verdicts.decisive_quote: Direct quantitative evidence for Meta's year-over-year revenue growth or its acceleration in the fiscal quarter ending 2025-03-31 is unavailable. Leading indicators provide directional context but not magnitude.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Best-grounded and most mechanism-rich trace — it correctly flags that the predicate is an absolute YoY level rather than an acceleration, names both up-factors (Q4 beat, IAB/CNBC ad-market strength, AI monetisation) and down-factors (April-2024 guidance shock, TikTok share loss) with real E1 citations, but after declaring both boundary intervals merely 'plausible' it still tilts 0.75 to 'no' on an unargued central estimate of 5 percent.

verdicts.decisive_quote: it lacks specific year-over-year revenue growth percentages for either quarter, preventing a precise assessment of whether the 20.63% threshold or the acceleration condition will be met.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Honest about having only headline-level qualitative evidence and its reasoning does point at 'no', but it then converts a single 'muted outlook' headline into a 5/12/18 percent band, calls the 'yes' interval outright 'unsupported', and raises confidence to 0.8 in the same block where it declares magnitude support insufficient.

verdicts.decisive_quote: the weight of evidence supporting strong momentum suggests the year-over-year revenue growth is likely to meet or exceed the 20.63% threshold
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Invents no figures and its nodes map to real E0 headlines, but the entire graph is directional and never produces any level estimate, so the load-bearing step from 'strong momentum' to 'at least 20.63 percent' is pure assertion and the trace never admits that gap.

verdicts.decisive_quote: The positive market trends, successful AI integration, and strong prior quarter performance suggest Meta's revenue growth could meet or exceed the 20.63% threshold, but this is not directly confirmed by Q1 2025 specific data.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: Every substantive step is marked 'up' and the target bridge says the drivers suggest the threshold could be met, yet the forecast silently substitutes a 15 percent central estimate with basis 'insufficient' and predicts 'no' — the narrative and the selection point opposite ways, and the two blocks even disagree on the probabilities (0.30/0.70 vs 0.35/0.65).

verdicts.decisive_quote: Meta Platforms, Inc. reported year-over-year revenue growth of 25% for the fourth quarter of 2024, which is above the 20.63% threshold specified in the resolution rule.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: The whole forecast hangs on a fabricated 25 percent Q4 2024 growth rate attributed to two E0 items that are headline-only and contain no numbers; the downstream logic and boundary check are coherent, which makes the invention more damaging, and it labels magnitude support 'insufficient' while still putting 0.75 on 'yes'.

verdicts.decisive_quote: Using Q1 2024 revenue of $36.45B (external context implied by guidance analysis) and the midpoint of Q1 2025 guidance ($33.125B), Q1 2025 YoY growth is estimated at -9.1%.
verdicts.verdict_one_line: A precise-looking arithmetic chain built entirely on invented inputs — a 23 percent Q3 figure, an inferred 25 percent Q4 figure, a $32B-$34.25B Q1 2025 guidance range and a $36.45B prior-year base, none of which appear anywhere in E0 — yielding an implausible -9.1 percent revenue decline for a company its own evidence calls record-setting, and then 0.95 confidence on top of self-declared 'weak' support.

ranking_rationale: Both banks contain only headlines with no revenue figures at all, so the separator was whether a trace admitted that no quantity was available and sized its confidence accordingly, or manufactured one: principle_memory and hgf named the missing datum, reasoned from real cited drivers to the boundary, and stayed near 0.7, while direct_forecast and case_memory fabricated growth rates and guidance ranges that appear in neither bank and then leaned on them hard. In the middle, structured_reasoning and factor_memory stayed clean on facts but broke on the bridge - one asserted the 20.63 percent threshold would be cleared with no level estimate at all, the other argued 'up' throughout and then predicted 'no'.
shared_evidence_note: The E0 and E1 banks are nearly interchangeable for this question - both are numberless headline snippets and E1 merely adds ad-market and competitive-landscape colour - so the yes/no split came from how each trace handled the shared absence of any magnitude anchor, not from reading different evidence.
